Multiply the singular values $\sigma_i$ into $B_i(\beta)$ so that $B_i(\beta) \leftarrow \sigma_i B_i(\beta)$ [S1].

The claim states that singular values $σ_i$ are multiplied into $B_i(β)$ such that $B_i(β) ← σ_i B_i(β)$. The evidence in Source [S1] explicitly states: 'The singular values from the SVD are multiplied into Bi.' Additionally, the mathematical approximation provided is $I(γ, β) ≈ ∑_i^N Γ_i(γ) B_i(β)$, where the SVD of the sampled matrix yields components $Γ_i$, $B_i$, and singular values $σ_i$. In standard SVD notation $A = UΣV^T$, the columns of $U$ and $V$ are the singular vectors, and $Σ$ contains the singular values. To reconstruct the matrix (or function) from the normalized singular vectors, the singular values must be absorbed into one of the vector sets. The text confirms this operation by stating the singular values are multiplied into $B_i$.
